name: Pale Turquoise
lede: Pale Turquoise is a light, greenish-blue tint of turquoise, best known as a web color and as the wrong answer to the question of what color the universe is.

sections.title: A web color
sections.body:
PaleTurquoise is one of the named colors in the X11 set, with the hex code #AFEEEE, and it passed into CSS from there [1]. Our library also holds a second reading from the 2010 xkcd survey, #A5FBD5, a greener and brighter mint than the web color [2]. The ISCC-NBS system calls the web swatch a very light bluish green, 7.2 units away on the CIEDE2000 scale [2].

The name is simply "pale" added to [[turquoise]], so it carries the stone's history only at one remove. Its neighbors are [[aqua]], [[celeste]] and [[mint]] [2].

sections.title: The color of the universe
sections.body:
In the early 2000s astronomers at Johns Hopkins University announced a color for the light of the whole universe, and the press reported it as pale turquoise [3][4]. Maggie Nelson's *Bluets* recalls reading that news and taking it as proof that the world's heart is blue [4]. The announcement was wrong. A computer error had skewed the calculation, and the true figure was closer to beige, the co-author Karl Glazebrook admitted [3][5].

The calculation asked what you would see if you could gather all the light from some 200,000 galaxies into a box [3]. The story is a good myth to know about: the universe is not turquoise, and a pale turquoise claim should be treated as a corrected error [3][5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color near this swatch appears in 5 works, or 0.02 per cent, which is rarer than 77 per cent of the named colors [6]. The earliest match is a view by Canaletto from 1748, and the latest is from 1904 [6]. That is 262 years before the name's first record in our sources, so these are look-alike hues in aged photographs, not evidence of a pigment [6]. In printed English the word peaks in the 2010s [6].

questions.q: What was the corrected color of the universe, after the pale turquoise claim?
True or false: the universe is pale turquoise.

openers: The universe was once reported to be pale turquoise; the number was a computer error and the corrected color was beige.
Pale Turquoise is #AFEEEE, a named color in the X11 set that CSS inherited.
